instruction: Align the titles to the center on slides 1, 2, and 3.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires center-aligning titles in slides 1, 2, and 3. Evaluator uses custom getter to extract text alignment from title paragraphs and custom metric to verify all three slides have center alignment. Slide titles are: Slide 1='Goal Roadmap', Slide 2='How to Use This Presentation', Slide 3='Add a Roadmap Page'.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Each correctly aligned slide contributes 1/3 to the final score (partial credit enabled)

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all three requirements: center alignment for slide 1, 2, and 3 titles
Metric function correctly handles expected parameter when type='rule' - accesses expected.get('slide_alignments') directly since expected IS the rules dictionary
Getter extracts title alignment using python-pptx library and maps PP_ALIGN enum to strings correctly
Partial credit logic is sound: each correctly aligned slide contributes 1/3 to final score
Postconfig appropriately saves file with Ctrl+S to ensure changes are persisted before verification
Data flow is semantically correct: getter returns {slide_idx: alignment_string}, metric compares against expected alignments
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Title detection uses heuristic 'first shape with text' which may fail on non-standard slide layouts. Consider using 'slide.shapes.title' property instead for more robust title placeholder detection
Getter could handle edge case where title shape exists but has no paragraphs with text (currently would not add entry to result dict)
